column1: # The routes and what must hold on each replay: tools/check_routes.py (ctest oracles-routes, with ORACLES_ROM_DIR set).

# exploration.route with the objects' animation stepped from the fan game's tables against the live game (--object-animation-check): every pose change of the interactions at their place a neighbour animates by the rule is the game's, both ways; the probe's verdict is never the other of the game's first updates after a scroll; every pose shown live has its tiles in the capture.  The rooms its captures hold show enemies (frozen in a neighbour) and objects whose code does not advance their animation there: nothing a neighbour animates.

# exploration.route in the far view with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel), the default on computers, as Gifts of Kinomi and Temple of Seasons have one: the camera and Link at their fraction of a pixel through its 52 scrolls, nothing of the band or of his layer left behind or drawn wrong.
# exploration.route with the rooms never visited kept dark (--unvisited-rooms hidden): the game's record of the rooms entered on Moonrise Regalia's profile.

# exploration.route in Far 4:3, the view of a 640x480 handheld: the animated objects counted at each delivery of their room (enhanced.poses_animated), whose chain runs again less often since the visited bits of other rooms are aside when its parents are judged (28, 30 before), and the pose changes drawn (50 on SameBoy, 48 on mGBA, where the deliveries fall otherwise; poses_drawn_wrong=0 on both).
# exploration.route in the view's other sizes (docs/REFERENCE.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.

# exploration.route with the status bar drawn full width (--hud full, the launcher's default hud=full): the bands beside it take its own background on every line of every world frame, far and far 4:3.

# exploration.route with Text size Large and Very large (--text-size, the counters of ages/checks.tsv): the game's box enlarged from the core's image, as in Ages and Seasons, on the 969 frames of a text (970 on mGBA), 334 of them over the framed core; the box the host draws compared with the core's on each of them (--text-box-check); the live state that of its row without them.

# exploration.route with the transitions' diagonal (--continuous-diagonal): the game goes elsewhere from 5665 on, where Link walking down into 0:44 stops on the pixel the game's distance ends on while the room loads, a pixel short of where the route's transitions took him; its diagonals held then carry him through two scrolls (transitions.carried_frames, enhanced.scrolls_diagonal), walls across holding him in others (carry_withheld_frames); the sprite's steps back (enhanced.link_backsteps) all fall outside those scrolls, in normal play, as on the route without the option.
# With the settling camera Link's sprite goes back on the screen against the step before 4 times across and once down (enhanced.link_backsteps, _y), the previous camera 5 and 5.

# The compact text (--text compact, Enhanced alone), Moonrise's English laid out again in the banks its profile leaves to a language (the counters of ages/checks.tsv: text.laid_out, text.layout_failed none, text.boxes for text.boxes_laid_out) and drawn by the transaction at the profile's routines: compact-exploration.route, exploration.route's keys moved for the dialogues the compact text closes sooner (its comment), the same rooms; its dialogues' lines in the font's own widths, none past 128 pixels, the reveal to the pixel (none cut or early), the box where the game drew it.
# exploration.route with the status bar laid out (--hud wide): Moonrise Regalia's bar is the base game's, laid out in every world frame.

# exploration.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel) in the near view, measured: its large rooms (8 scrolls between them) and the diagonals walked there and outdoors (915 frames). Drawn at his exact place, Link on the ground no longer steps across then down in turn on a diagonal (enhanced.link_wobble, 200 without the option); the five left are the game's own steps, the camera still, Link's speed changing on the diagonal (15927: one pixel across on a frame without one down).

# The wide text box (--text-box wide, the counters of ages/checks.tsv), Moonrise's English laid out again at 192 pixels, classic at the game's fixed advance and compact (text.boxes as the game lays them out, text.boxes_laid_out as served: a box in five fewer classic, a box in three fewer compact): each frame the box shows, its text against its layout's glyphs, none wrong, none uncovered, cut or early, none past 192 pixels; the pages the game keeps laid out for its 128 pixels centred. The route's keys depend on the pages: past its first dialogue, closed in fewer boxes, the replay goes its own way, the same on each, through fewer rooms (transitions.taken).

# ammo.route: exploration.route's keys, then by hand at its end a bomb dropped (17510), its blast taken; --poke-at gives Link, whose game has none, five bombs on B at 17505 (wInventoryB, wNumBombs, the bombs' obtained flag set beside the game's). With --cheats ammo the bomb is kept; with every cheat the hits of the route and the blast cost no heart, every point armed. No route of Moonrise has a purchase: its rupees' point is held by oracles-cheats-roms, which calls its removeRupeeValue in the core.
